section_summary: This section records the final arrangements for dividing former Japanese combatant vessels among the United States, Britain, China and the Soviet Union, including the designation of representatives and delivery ports. It also documents Australia's objection, plans for disposing of the U.S. share, and France's eventual refusal of four destroyers. The closing pages contain copies of earlier diplomatic notes assembled for the State-War-Navy Coordinating Committee.

subfiles.title: Cover letter forwarding Soviet note to Secretary of War
subfiles.about: Forwards a translation of the Soviet note on allocating former Japanese naval vessels.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the May 17 Soviet note.

subfiles.title: Cover letter forwarding Soviet note to Secretary of the Navy
subfiles.about: Forwards the Soviet note on allocating former Japanese naval vessels.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the May 17 Soviet note.

subfiles.title: Secretary's instruction on Australian Ambassador
subfiles.about: Conveys approval for explaining the fleet partition to the Australian Ambassador.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary approves Vincent's recommendation.

subfiles.title: Recommendation concerning Australian inquiry
subfiles.about: Seeks approval for Hilldring to explain why the four-power division should proceed.
subfiles.summary: Vincent recommends briefing the Australian Ambassador and declining to reopen the agreement.

subfiles.title: Visit of Australian Ambassador on May 13 With Regard to the Division of the Japanese Fleet
subfiles.about: Reviews the history of the four-power agreement and recommends a response to Australia's request.
subfiles.summary: Vincent traces the decision to destroy large Japanese warships and divide smaller combatants among four powers. He recommends telling Ambassador Makin that preparations are complete and revision or delay until a peace conference is impracticable.

subfiles.title: Telegram urging Chinese reply on ship division
subfiles.about: Requests urgent Chinese agreement, a representative and a delivery port.
subfiles.summary: Asks the embassy to expedite China's formal reply so ship division can proceed.

subfiles.title: Australian position with regard to division of Japanese Navy
subfiles.about: Records Hilldring and Vincent's explanation to Australian Minister Stirling.
subfiles.summary: Stirling was told that the United States sympathized with Australia's wish to participate in Pacific settlements but would not seek to revise the long-standing four-power agreement. He undertook to report the decision to Canberra.

subfiles.title: Airgram transmitting Soviet representative's designation
subfiles.to: U.S. Political Adviser to SCAP, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Transmits the Soviet note naming Rear Admiral Stetsenko.
subfiles.summary: Stetsenko and six others departed for Japan to receive the Soviet share.

subfiles.title: Urgent telegram on delayed Chinese reply
subfiles.about: Urges the embassy to obtain China's formal response despite its representatives' arrival in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: The formal Chinese reply is needed before drawing lots or deciding the U.S. share.

subfiles.title: Chinese designation of allocation representatives
subfiles.about: Names two Chinese Navy captains and Shanghai as the delivery port.
subfiles.summary: Designates Ma Te-Chien and Yao Yu for the drawing of lots.

subfiles.title: Nanking report on Chinese representatives
subfiles.about: Relays the Chinese Foreign Office's designation of representatives and Shanghai.
subfiles.summary: Reports China's telephone notification naming two captains and Shanghai.

subfiles.title: Status of Division of Japanese Ships
subfiles.about: Reviews the expected drawing of lots and pending approval of SWNCC 186/27.
subfiles.summary: The Chinese note permits division; the U.S. share's disposal awaits SWNCC approval and legal advice.

subfiles.title: Chinese acceptance of amended vessel division plan
subfiles.about: Accepts the division and delivery plan in the February and April U.S. notes.
subfiles.summary: China formally accepts the amended four-power plan.

subfiles.title: French Uncertainty as to Acceptance of Four Former Japanese Destroyers
subfiles.about: Sets an August 8 deadline for France to decide whether to accept four demilitarized destroyers.
subfiles.summary: France doubts their civilian value and must answer before the final drawing.

subfiles.title: Record-copy replacement notice
subfiles.about: Marks a telegram copy as the record copy because the action copy was not returned.
subfiles.summary: Designates the white copy as the replacement record copy.

subfiles.title: Nanking report on Chinese representatives, information copy
subfiles.about: Duplicates the Chinese Foreign Office report on representatives and Shanghai.
subfiles.summary: Information copy of the June 6 telegram.

subfiles.title: Telegram transmitting Chinese Ambassador's designation
subfiles.about: Transmits the Chinese note naming Ma Te-Chien and Yao Yu and selecting Shanghai.
subfiles.summary: Provides Tokyo the Chinese Ambassador's formal designation.

subfiles.title: Cover letter forwarding Chinese note to Secretary of War
subfiles.about: Forwards the June 9 Chinese Ambassador's note on Japanese combatant vessels.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the Chinese note already transmitted to Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Cover letter forwarding Chinese note to Secretary of the Navy
subfiles.about: Forwards the June 9 Chinese Ambassador's note.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the Chinese designation and delivery-port note.

subfiles.title: Chinese Embassy address sheet
subfiles.about: Addresses correspondence to the chief of the Division of Chinese Affairs.
subfiles.summary: Chinese Embassy address sheet.

subfiles.title: Chinese designation of allocation representatives
subfiles.about: Names Ma Te-Chien and Yao Yu and selects Shanghai as the delivery port.
subfiles.summary: Formal Chinese designation for drawing lots and receiving ships.

subfiles.title: Nanking telegram on Chinese Embassy instructions
subfiles.about: Reports that the Chinese Embassy in Washington was instructed to accept the U.S. procedure.
subfiles.summary: The Foreign Office says concurrence, representatives and port were sent to Washington.

subfiles.title: Nanking telegram on Chinese Foreign Office note
subfiles.about: Reports China's written acceptance, representatives and Shanghai delivery port.
subfiles.summary: Relays the Foreign Office's June 12 note accepting the February 24 procedure.

subfiles.title: Cover letter forwarding June 19 Chinese note
subfiles.about: Forwards China's acceptance of the vessel division plan.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the June 19 Chinese note.

subfiles.title: Copy of Chinese acceptance note
subfiles.about: Accepts the amended arrangements for dividing and delivering Japanese vessels.
subfiles.summary: Copy of China's formal acceptance.

subfiles.title: Airgram transmitting Chinese acceptance
subfiles.to: U.S. Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Transmits the June 19 Chinese note accepting the vessel plan.
subfiles.summary: Quotes China's formal acceptance for the political adviser.

subfiles.title: SWNCC transmittal of approved 186/27
subfiles.about: Transmits the approved U.S.-share disposal plan and requests action on French and Chinese transfers.
subfiles.summary: Requests legal clearance, recipient agreements without future U.S. liability, and a report to SWNCC.

subfiles.title: Decision amending SWNCC 186/27, first copy
subfiles.about: Records approval of the vessel disposal plan and no-recourse terms for foreign transfers.
subfiles.summary: Directs replacement of revised pages and notification to military commands.

subfiles.title: Decision amending SWNCC 186/27, copy 52
subfiles.about: Duplicates the decision approving the amended disposal plan.
subfiles.summary: Copy 52 of the July 22 amendment decision.

subfiles.title: Disposition of U.S. Share of Ex-Japanese Combatant Vessels
subfiles.from: SWNCC Subcommittee for the Far East
subfiles.about: Proposes priorities for the U.S. share of former Japanese combatant vessels.
subfiles.summary: The report reviews French claims, Chinese interest, scrap shortages, Japanese economic uses and Navy target needs. Its revised conclusions offer four destroyers to France and two destroyers plus three escorts to China if legally transferable, reserve selected vessels as targets, return useful slow vessels to Japanese commerce, and scrap the remainder in Japan. Foreign transfers require agreement and legal clearance.

subfiles.title: Recommendation after French refusal of destroyers
subfiles.from: J. H. Hilldring, State Department member of SWNCC
subfiles.about: Recommends alternative disposal after France refused its destroyers and questions a Chinese transfer.
subfiles.summary: France declined its four vessels because they were costly to restore and of little commercial value. The memorandum judges the proposed Chinese vessels similarly burdensome and recommends disposing of both portions under SWNCC 186/27's other priorities.

subfiles.title: French refusal of former Japanese vessels
subfiles.about: Declines the U.S. offer of former Japanese vessels because restoration would be costly.
subfiles.summary: France thanks the United States but declines the vessels as uneconomic to operate or sell.

subfiles.title: Disposition of Combatant Vessels of the Japanese Navy
subfiles.about: Summarizes diplomatic exchanges accepting vessel division and forwards copies to SWNCC members.
subfiles.summary: Hilldring lists U.S., Soviet, British and Chinese notes on ship division, delivery and scrapping. He concludes that all three recipient governments accepted the proposed procedure, including scrapping ships that cannot readily be made operable, and asks that the enclosures reach War and Navy members.

subfiles.title: U.S. note to Soviet Ambassador on division procedure
subfiles.about: Sets out the four-power allocation, delivery and scrapping procedure.
subfiles.summary: The note calls for scrapping inoperable ships, drawing lots for demilitarized vessels, naming a representative and one delivery port, and reimbursing U.S. supplies used in delivery.

subfiles.title: Soviet acceptance and Nakhodka designation
subfiles.about: Accepts immediate division, selects Nakhodka and requests information on larger warships.
subfiles.summary: The Soviet government will send a representative and seeks details on larger Japanese vessels.

subfiles.title: U.S. reply on larger Japanese warships
subfiles.about: Explains the destruction of Japanese vessels larger than destroyers.
subfiles.summary: The larger ships have been or are being scrapped under SCAP directives; details are available in Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Soviet designation of Rear Admiral Stetsenko
subfiles.about: Names Stetsenko as the Soviet representative for allocating and receiving vessels.
subfiles.summary: Stetsenko and six accompanying persons have left for Japan.

subfiles.title: British inquiry on auxiliary vessels
subfiles.about: Asks about Japanese tugs, harbor craft, salvage vessels and technical details of listed ships.
subfiles.summary: Britain requests disposal plans and vessel specifications.

subfiles.title: U.S. reply on Japanese auxiliary vessels
subfiles.about: Explains that noncombatant auxiliary vessels will support Japan's economic rehabilitation.
subfiles.summary: The vessels are excluded from combatant division; Britain should seek further technical data from SCAP.

subfiles.title: British acceptance and delivery-port request
subfiles.about: Accepts the division procedure while seeking delivery to Singapore or Hong Kong.
subfiles.summary: Britain names its naval adviser to draw lots and requests a Japanese crew repatriation ship.

subfiles.title: Chinese designation of allocation representatives, copy
subfiles.about: Names Chinese representatives and Shanghai as delivery port.
subfiles.summary: Copy of the Chinese designation of Ma Te-Chien and Yao Yu.

subfiles.title: Chinese acceptance of division procedure, copy
subfiles.about: Accepts the amended four-power division and delivery plan.
subfiles.summary: Copy of China's formal acceptance.

subfiles.title: U.S. note to Soviet Ambassador on division procedure, second copy
subfiles.about: Restates the proposed allocation, delivery and scrapping procedure.
subfiles.summary: Second copy of the February 24 note, including the request for a Soviet representative and Far Eastern delivery port.
